title: Integers With Multiple Sum of Two Cubes
summary: Given an integer n, find all integers x less than or equal to n for which there exist at least two distinct pairs of positive integers (a, b) such that a <= b and x = a^3 + b^3.
statement: Given an integer n, find all integers x less than or equal to n for which there exist at least two distinct pairs of positive integers (a, b) such that a <= b and x = a^3 + b^3. Return these integers in ascending order.
constraints: n is positive and at most 1,000,000,000.
Use positive integers a≤b and count distinct pairs satisfying x=a³+b³.
Return ascending x≤n that have at least two such pairs.
hints: Both cube bases are bounded by the cube root of n.
Enumerate a≤b, stop each inner loop once the sum exceeds n, and count each sum.
Filter counts greater than one and sort the keys.
The ordering constraint makes every mathematical pair appear once, so the counts exactly measure distinct representations.
editorial: The ordering constraint makes every mathematical pair appear once, so the counts exactly measure distinct representations.

tests.explanation: 1729 and 4104 each have two distinct positive cube-pair representations.
1729=1³+12³=9³+10³, so it is the first returned value.
